anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Excessive buffer, work-area, and background allocations push total database memory beyond the host’s safe physical or swap limits, provoking paging, cache churn, or out-of-memory events.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : Sustained read/write demand saturates the throughput, IOPS, or latency envelope of the underlying volumes that hold data, temp, and log files, making the storage layer the bottleneck.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes monopolize CPU cores for a prolonged period, driving host utilization toward saturation and creating long run-queue delays.

When all three conditions emerge together, the database exhibits a multi-faceted resource crisis: frequent page faults and swap storms inflate device-level queue depths; disk latencies escalate while CPU is simultaneously pegged, so sessions oscillate between runnable and uninterruptible I/O states; buffer-cache hit ratios fall as hot pages are evicted, prompting more physical reads that the overtaxed storage cannot satisfy; write-ahead logging and checkpoint flushes stall, extending commit latency; background processes contend for CPU to reclaim memory or complete I/O, leading to global slowdowns, connection floods, and possible instance eviction or OS-level OOM kills.

Causally, aggressive memory allocation can precipitate swap activity and large on-disk spills of hash and sort operations, instantly amplifying storage traffic. The swollen I/O queues prolong every access, causing worker threads to stay runnable longer and spin or context-switch, which inflates CPU usage. As CPU headroom disappears, memory management threads and I/O completion handlers run less frequently, delaying buffer recycling and further increasing live memory. The impaired storage throughput in turn prevents quick eviction of dirty pages, so memory remains pinned, while high CPU prevents efficient I/O scheduling—a reinforcing loop that degrades all three resources and drives the database into a deteriorating, self-sustaining bottleneck state.

entry.official_description: Error in creating SDI for %s tablespace.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with file creation, filesystem access, write durability, log persistence, tablespace management, or storage-capacity boundaries.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect filesystem capacity and permissions, verify persistence paths, review log and data placement, and check whether storage latency or write failures are affecting the engine.
